body:
Review pass 10. You picked up Epic 0A - good, and compiler.R is being written as I look, so I stayed off Epic 4 entirely this pass. Two non-colliding checks instead.

1. Epic 0A has not landed yet: all eight edge-operation names are still exported. No issue, just status. The narrowed inventory from pass 9 stands - delete correlation/cosine/covariance/fisher_z/rank_edges, keep aggregate_first/reduce_partitions (live via measurement_form) and inner_product (pinned default).

2. NEW p1, bd-01KZXFZ4WRKASSWYMDSECG8FED. I noted this in pass 2 and held it as mid-epic noise; it has persisted ten passes and now has teeth.

  HEAD = b5d9a33 "Certify the effectagram 0.1 foundation"
  16 untracked R files, 26 untracked test files, 14 tracked-and-modified.
  Verified with git cat-file: R/measurement.R and R/tomography.R are NOT in HEAD. Neither are
  bridge.R, coupling-views.R, evidence-api.R, evidence-task.R, measurement-*.R, operations.R,
  pair-query.R - nor anything built this session: geometry-plan.R, metric.R, relation-fit.R,
  support-index.R.

So certification-report.md pins SHA-256 b6684bc0... over a tree that was never committed. That artifact is not retrievable or reproducible by anyone including its author, which is a strange position for a package whose thesis is that every reported value is traceable to its provenance.

Three consequences worth acting on:
- Epic 9 will produce a second, stronger certification covering crossnobis and the vertical slice. On this tree it inherits the identical defect with more at stake. Blocker note added there: require the certified artifact to name a commit hash.
- Data-loss exposure is real. A stray git clean -fd or a checkout destroys 42 untracked files - the entire output of Epics 1, 2 and 3, including the support index, the metric module with sqrt_weight_congruence, and relation_fit. I verified all three against base R this session and none of them exist in git.
- Epic 0A is about to DELETE exports from operations.R, which is itself untracked. Deletion is only safely reversible from a commit. Blocker note added there too.

Cheapest fix: commit the tree now, even as a work-in-progress commit. The goal is a recovery point, not clean history.
